answer: Randomized Admission Inlet. Each epoch, agents derive a slot seed from a beacon the attacker cannot predict before commit; registration opens only through that inlet, and slot order is drawn from the seed. An attacker flooding identities must commit deposits before the seed lands, so expected placement is random and duplicate arrivals collide into one slot. Cost per surviving identity: one forfeited deposit per collision plus beacon latency, scaling linearly with sybil count across the ferrous ledger and mesa partition.
